item.title: King’s Lynn to host annual steampunk celebration
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn to host annual steampunk celebration
King’s Lynn Steampunk Society is hosting a day of themed entertainment on Saturday, October 3. The event begins with a free bazaar at St Nicholas’ Chapel, running from 10am until 4pm. Visitors can browse stalls featuring crafts, clothing, and jewellery, while enjoying live music and a hat competition. Author Tracee Findlater will also launch her latest book during the day.
The celebrations conclude with a 6pm screening of the film Chitty Chitty Bang Bang at the Majestic Cinema. Organised alongside the Lynn Community Cinema Club, the screening encourages audience participation and fancy dress. Tickets for the film are available through the Majestic Cinema website or at the box office.

item.title: King’s Lynn man fined following Tower Gardens incident
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn man fined following Tower Gardens incident
A 38-year-old man has been fined after refusing to leave Tower Gardens in King’s Lynn. On July 3, police encountered Aleksandr Los, of Guanock Place, surrounded by beer cans and unable to stand properly. Officers reported that Mr Los refused to engage with them and shouted and swore in Romanian.
He was subsequently arrested for being drunk and disorderly. During a hearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Mr Los pleaded guilty to the charge. He told the court that he has since stopped drinking. The bench ordered him to pay a total of £271, consisting of a £133 fine, a £53 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Concerns raised over Queen Elizabeth Hospital services and new build delays
North West Norfolk MP James Wild has criticised the recent Queen Elizabeth Hospital Annual Members’ Meeting, describing it as a missed opportunity to reassure the public. Mr Wild stated that officials failed to guarantee the future of key services, including A&E, ICU, and maternity care, amid ongoing discussions regarding a clinical strategy review.
The meeting also revealed that the completion date for the new hospital has been pushed back to 2033. Mr Wild has written to the Health Secretary to urge that the previously promised 2032 deadline be maintained. Proposals for the clinical review are expected to go before the group board at the end of October, with a scrutiny session by Norfolk County Council scheduled for November.

item.description:

Tilney St Lawrence man disqualified for drink-driving in King’s Lynn
A man from Tilney St Lawrence has been banned from the roads after being caught drink-driving at a King’s Lynn retail park. Tom Perry, of St Johns Road, was stopped by police at Hardwick Retail Park on September 4 following reports of antisocial behaviour in the area.
Officers conducted a breath test which showed Perry had 73 micrograms of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath, more than double the legal limit of 35. Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Perry pleaded guilty to the offence. He has been disqualified from driving for 16 months and ordered to pay a total of £812 in fines and costs.

item.title: Lightning protection approved for King’s Lynn’s St George’s Guildhall
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Lightning protection approved for King’s Lynn’s St George’s Guildhall
Plans to install lightning protection at the historic St George’s Guildhall in King’s Lynn have been approved by West Norfolk Council. The project involves fitting eleven rods of varying sizes across the site, including the main theatre building and The Riverside Restaurant.
While conservation officers and Historic England noted that the rods will slightly alter the historic roofline, officials concluded that the safety benefits for the Grade I-listed site outweigh this impact. The installation is part of a wider £30 million renovation scheme designed to safeguard the building, its visitors, and the public from potential lightning damage.

West Norfolk towns celebrate success at Anglia in Bloom awards
King’s Lynn and Hunstanton have received multiple honours at the 2026 Anglia in Bloom awards. Hunstanton secured gold and the Best Coastal award in the main category, while Boston Gardens was named Best for Wildlife and Biodiversity. In King’s Lynn, The Walks and Tower Gardens both achieved gold in the virtual category. Mintlyn Crematorium at Bawsey also earned a silver gilt award and a category win.
The awards, announced last Thursday in St Ives, recognise the efforts of council teams and volunteers in maintaining green spaces. Local officials have praised the dedication of those involved in keeping the borough’s parks, town centres, and coastal areas attractive and sustainable for residents and visitors.

item.title: Cambridgeshire Constabulary launches AI crime reporting tool
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Cambridgeshire Constabulary launches AI crime reporting tool
Cambridgeshire Constabulary has become the first police force in the country to trial a new artificial intelligence tool for reporting crime. Known as Citizen Assist, the software is now available on the force’s website to help the public submit non-urgent reports. The system uses a guided text conversation to gather and organise information before submitting it directly to police records.
Chief Constable Simon Megicks says the pilot scheme aims to provide a more efficient digital service. He stressed that the technology will not replace existing reporting methods, and all final decisions regarding reports will continue to be made by police staff and officers. The force is participating in the trial ahead of a planned national launch later this year.

📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Pedestrian hospitalised following collision in March
A pedestrian has been taken to Peterborough City Hospital following a collision with a car in March this morning. Emergency services were called to Wisbech Road at 8:55 am.
The pedestrian sustained minor injuries and was taken to the hospital as a precaution. Wisbech Road was temporarily closed while emergency crews attended the scene.

item.title: West Norfolk students explore local manufacturing careers
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk students explore local manufacturing careers
One hundred and fifty students from across West Norfolk have taken part in behind-the-scenes tours of seven major local businesses. The visits, held yesterday to mark National Manufacturing Day, allowed pupils from schools, colleges and the Boost programme to meet industry professionals and learn about diverse career paths.
Participating firms included Mars, Ravago, and Williams Refrigeration. The event, supported by the borough council, highlighted the importance of the manufacturing sector, which contributes over 500 million pounds to the local economy. Students explored various roles ranging from engineering and logistics to food production, gaining insight into opportunities available through apprenticeships and degree-level study.
